newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower after CBOT falters.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower after CBOT falters.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended weaker after their CBOT counterparts faltered late, traders said.
"The buying just kind of ran out. March had been bid at $4.06, and then when Chicago broke, everyone started selling it at $4.06," a KCBT trader said.
Traders said KCBT wheat was under pressure early after cash basis bids softened at the Gulf of Mexico and at mill locations in eastern Kansas.
"The market's on a nice bulge and we're starting to see some wheat move out of the country," a trader said at midday.
But a bullish export lineup and strength in CBOT wheat pushed KCBT wheat values off their lows at the midsession.
KCBT wheat closed 2-1/2 to six cents per bushel lower, with Dec down 2-1/2 cents at $4.32-1/2. The Dec/March spread closed at 29-1/2 cents, after trading between 28-1/2 and 29-1/2 cents all day.

Traders said CIS sold two million March bushels and bought 900,000 March and one million Dec. E D & F Man International sold one million March and bought 1.5 million Dec. Prudential sold one million March.
Continental bull-spread 500,000 Dec/March at 28-1/2 to 29 cents. Prudential bear-spread 800,000 March/Dec in the same range.
